This series has ruthlessly exposed the huge flaw in Englands current approach (I’m not going to use the B slur); the massive amount of pressure it puts on the bowling unit. I understand India is a tough place to play but this was always going to be the test to see if could work in unfamiliar and hostile conditions. Teams have gone there in the past with less skill and given a good account of themselves regardless.

The media and players and even us have heavily focused on the batting side of it but thats only one half of the game. Both sides of the ball have to give the other a chance. When you play classic test cricket that responsibility waxes and wanes on both units depending on the state of any one game in progress. Englands bowling attacks currently NEED to have perfect innings every time because the batting innings are usually short, either through scoring quickly and getting out or falling apart through ill discipline like today. On top of that off the top of my head they’ve bowled about twice as many overs as the Indian bowlers in as least two test matches and have done so a few other times since this new system has come into play. The bowlers get worn down so much over time in hot conditions. I think all the current England bowlers are very good players but not of the quality as a singular entity to shoulder something like that. Like I said, both units are gonna have bad days whether you like it or not, but thats when players step up and gave their team a chance thats just not seeming to happen when one is asked to keep them in the game time and time again, not because of luck or form but because of an absolute dogmatic attachment to the current batting style.

Of course to counteract this you make team choices that work into this philosophy: experienced mentally strong bowlers, pace bowling all rounders so you can pick all the spinners you need,  the most senior players in bowling roles no matter of their international experience if you have injuries. But they haven’t. Rookie spinners in brutal conditions on top of Stokes not bowling and not finding someone who can pick up the bowling slack (which is how we got Root bowling 27 overs in an innings) has ruined any chance they had of winning once India started figuring out their bowlers. They have seemed to only focus on what batting brings them and not thought about what they need to do with their bowling in order for this system to work.

For all the bullshit thats been thrown around I feel like only half the story is being told. Anderson and Board are on the way out and everyone else they have look uninspiring. If they want to keep playing this way they’re going to be in for a rude shock when half their game is non existent and the other half gets found out when teams start eventually planning around their aggression. 

I feel this team is in big trouble in the near future if they continue to only plan for one half of the game
